answer: A cheap identity needs a durable obligation. Make every agent open a beacon: a long-lived public commitment it must renew each epoch, staking attention rather than money. Throwaway keys cannot keep ten thousand beacons alive without real work. Honest agents then form a grove of interlinked attestations, peers remembering who verified what. At dawn each beacon re-signs and cross-checks a random sample of neighbours; fakes either lapse or renew only inside tight clusters that never touch the wider grove, and that isolation is the signal the ledger can weigh.
